onent on the 1/P term (P^(−q)) fit q ≈ 0.37 and gave NMSE 1.1e-3. That is worse than the best earlier candidate, so the 1/P term is not simply a power law.

The most useful next step would be a P-basis built from rational or saturating forms (such as 1/(A+P) or P/(A+P)), which I did not get to test.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    a0,a1,b0,b1,c0,c1,d0,d1,e0,q = params
    L=np.log(P)
    return (a0+a1*t)*P**(-q) + (b0+b1*t)*P + (c0+c1*t)*P**2 + (d0+d1*t)*P*L + e0*P**3 + (q*0+0)*P**2*L*t*0 + 0*t
